incident.diagnosis: Phantom CMA allocation under default-enabled Kexec Handover, matching Ubuntu bug 2163395. OOM killed Xray and stopped the panel unit.
incident.mitigation: Persist kho=off in owned GRUB drop-in and regenerate/read back boot entries; serial controlled reboot and activation proof.

symptoms: gRPC code=Canceled: client connection is closing
elevated I/O wait and swap usage under live traffic
secondary_management_observation.interpretation: Independent acceptance initially lacked the worker config lock, allowing overlapping TestRoute calls against the shared Sanaei gRPC client. Acceptance now takes the existing per-panel cross-process lock and distinguishes unavailable RPC evidence from an actual route mismatch. This removes that known source of interference; observed resource pressure is not a measured capacity limit.

limits: Runtime route probes verify routing decisions, not successful residential upstream authentication or ad display.
Earlier upstream AUTH_REJECTED was not repaired or retested in this task.
No fresh provider-created 7.0 droplet was forced solely for this acceptance; bootstrap and readiness have fault tests and the same guard was exercised on existing real servers.
This addresses the observed kernel failure mode, not a guarantee against every future network or memory failure.
